segments.text: In the last section, we put together our very first Docker file and then very quickly used it at the terminal to build a new image.
However, we didn't really talk about what was going on inside of here.
So in this section in the next, I want to do a deep dive on all the configuration that we added to the Docker file
and also what happened over at the terminal afterwards. So let's get to it.
Alright, so I took every line out of that Docker file except for the comments and put it into this diagram right here.
So you see from Alpine, Ron, and Command. You'll notice that every line of configuration we put in there look kind of similar to the others.
Every line started off with a single word that we refer to as an instruction.
This instruction is telling the Docker server to do some very specific preparation step on the image that we are trying to create.
The instruction from is used to specify the Docker image that we want to use as a base.
The run instruction is used to execute some command while we are preparing our custom image.
And then the CMD or command instruction specifies what should be executed when our container, or when our image is used to start up a brand new container.
Every line of configuration that you are ever going to add to a Docker file is always going to start off with an instruction.
Now, we just used the three most important instructions to know. There are quite another quite a handful of other instructions out there.
We're going to look at a handful of them throughout the rest of this course. But again, from Ron and CMD are the most important ones to know and understand.
After each instruction, we then provided an argument to the instruction that kind of customized how that instruction was executed.
So as my guess by putting from Alpine, we are saying we want to use a base image of Alpine when preparing our image.
And we'll talk more about exactly what that base image is doing for us in just a moment.
On the next one, we said, we want to run this command. This command was the argument that was provided to the instruction.
And then for CMD down here at the bottom, well, I bet you can guess yeah, that is the argument to CMD.
All right, so that's what was going on with the overall structure of the Docker file.
But that doesn't really explain a lot of the pieces or kind of like what the intent of each of these lines were outside of the comments that we added on there while we were writing the Docker file.
So let's take a quick pause. We're going to come back to the next section.

And we're going to start to look at the output that we got inside of our terminal and try to understand how each of those lines of configuration was interpreted by the Docker server and used to build our image.
So quick break and we'll see you in just a minute.
